text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

Plastic imports rose 79 percent in the first quarter of the year compared with the same period of 1996. The largest importers were local firms OPP, Politeno and Polialden, which purchased a major part of the 124,700 tonnes imported.
-- INDUSTRY SEEKS TO BE MORE COMPETITIVE
Speaking at a forum on the Real stabilization plan, Brazilian businessmen said they want new credit lines for exports and a new model for industry.

Brazil showed a $30 million trade deficit in the first three weeks of May. Exports totalled $2.58 billion, while imports amounted to $2.61 billion. So far this year, Brazil's trade deficit has totalled $4.03 billion.
-- CONGRESS MAY LEAVE RE-ELECTION PROBE FOR 1999

Opposition parties sent to Congress a request for a broad congressional inquiry into an alleged money-for-votes scam involving a re-election bill. But it may take two years for a parliamentary probe to be set up because the opposition does not have the number of signatures necessary for the bill to be approved immediately.
-- THREE HOMELESS KILLED IN CLASH WITH POLICE
Three men were killed and several were injured when 400 homeless families who had occupied a Sao Paulo low income housing project clashed with police sent to evict them.
-- KEY DAY FOR RE-ELECTION AND VOTE-BUYING PROBE IN CONGRESS

The federal government hopes the Senate will approve a bill allowing presidential re-election today. It also hopes to convince pro-government lawmakers who signed in favor of a broad congressional inquiry into an alleged cash-for-votes scam, to withdraw their signatures.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
